requirements.text: The system must support the exchange of 14 specific eProcurement documents: Catalogue, RFQ, Quotation, Purchase Order, PO Response, Fulfilment Notification, Receipt Advice, Rectification Advice, Invoice, Self Billed Invoice, Credit Note, Debit Note, Remittance Advice, and Statement.
All documents must be formatted as XML and validated using XML schema in compliance with the e-Government Interoperability Framework (e-GIF).
Every document must include a mandatory status attribute with values: original, copy, revision, or cancellation.

Every document must contain a mandatory Document UUID, Document ID, Document Date, Document Status, Test Status, Sender Software Manufacturer, Sender Software Product, Sender Software Version, and Schema Version.
The system must support Party identification using Party UUID, and include support for structured postal addresses based on BS 7666.
The system must support the use of international standard codes including ISO 3166 (country), ISO 4217 (currency), GLN, GTIN, and UNSPSC for commodity classification.
The system must support the use of Universally Unique Identifiers (UUID) for matching instances of Documents and Lines between different transactions.
The system must support the inclusion of digital signatures on document payloads using W3C Digital Signature standards.
The system must support the inclusion of attachments at both the Document and Line levels.
The system must support the definition of item aspects including name, value, and unit to capture domain-specific data.
The system must allow for incremental implementation of document types while maintaining backward compatibility and semantic consistency.
The system must provide a style sheet reference for each document to enable human-readable rendering for printing or display.
The system must support the inclusion of card verification values (CVV) and other payment security data when using Purchase Cards, while ensuring compliance with relevant data protection practices.
